_intro: Variety round 1, candidates only (nothing applied to the game). Plains hexes get an occasional small natural feature, plains hexes beside a road or town get an occasional lone cottage or pair of houses, and some road hexes get a building or trees beside the road. All of it is a visual choice made per hex from the static map (terrain, roads, sites), so the engine sees nothing. 39 kept candidates from 6 Codex sheets: 15 nature, 10 homestead, 14 roadside. Section 1 shows them on two real windows of a generated world (seed 1) with the shipped tiles first, then the three densities. Section 2 has every kept tile at 3x with its gate numbers. Section 3 has my first-pass picks and what applying would involve.
1. Board scale: before and after: Both windows are real exports of the seed 1 world (200 slots, scripts/road-study.py export): an open-country window with woods, ridges, one town and a factory, and a window with four towns, a three-way road junction at a town and four sites (factory, farm, oil field, steel mill). Rendered by scripts/board-mock.py with the frontend's tile rules, joins and the ratified site tiles, no grid. Units are composited by hand on the medium town render (board-mock draws no units), drawn the way WorldRenderer.placeUnitSprite does: 1.5 x HEX_SIZE wide, centred on the hex.

Measured shares on the whole seed 1 world (88,164 plains hexes; seed 2 within 0.01 of these): low decorates 7.9% of all plains hexes (nature on 5.1% of open plains, homesteads on 9.7% of plains beside a road or town and 16.7% beside a town, roadside on 6.7% of plains road hexes); medium 12.4% (nature 7.9%, homesteads 16.4% / 27.8% beside a town, roadside 9.0%); high 15.8% (nature 9.9%, homesteads 23.3% / 38.8% beside a town, roadside 9.1%). No two decorated hexes ever touch. Roadside barely grows from medium to high: along a road every hex has two road neighbours, so the no-neighbours rule caps it near one in ten.

With units on top: a unit sprite covers the middle three quarters of a hex. Every feature was painted off-centre, so most of a cottage or tree clump still shows beside the unit; a pair of houses or a tree row can be half hidden. Nothing competes with the unit for attention because the features are small and muted.
2. Candidates at 3x with gate results: Every kept tile passed the paint-in gates (registration, rim exact, rim clear, rim touch). Nature and homestead tiles sit on the G2 plains bases with the rim pinned to the base, so they abut any tile exactly like the shipped plains. Roadside tiles were painted over the shipped road tile itself, then the road and 3 px around it were put back from the shipped tile pixel for pixel (feathered 1.2 px beyond): road exact 0 and rim exact 0 on all 18 road cells, so the road's course, width, colour and its crossings at the hex edge are byte-identical to the shipped tile it varies. road clash counts painted pixels in the 4-7 px ring around the road (a building the hold would cut); the worst kept value is 8 px (straight_v-A, the cottage's shadow).

Mirrored shapes (straight_d, turn_n_se, turn_s_nw) reuse one file for both orientations, so their sheets also show each candidate as drawn mirrored. Nothing in them reads wrong mirrored (no text, no signs); the only change is that shadows fall lower-left instead of lower-right on the mirrored copy, the same compromise the shipped road tiles already make.

Dropped: two nature cells were too faint to read (a few px of blue glint for the damp hollow, a few pale specks for the wildflowers), one failed rim touch (a bramble thicket's shadow at the edge), and eight homestead cells were too close to the farm site (a lone barn with a yard, crop-row kitchen gardens, a house and big barn round a yard) or too small to read. Four roadside cells were fine but surplus to three per straight.
3. Notes: First-pass picks (above): 11 nature (trees, scrub, boulders, hedgerow, pond), 8 homesteads, and 13 roadside (3 per straight, 2 per turn except turn_n_se, where B's kitchen garden is painted as crop rows). Recommended density: medium. It puts something on about one plains hex in eight, a homestead on roughly one or two of the six hexes round each town, and reads as lived-in country without looking busy; low is nearly invisible at zoom 1, high starts to put a cottage beside most towns.

What does not work or needs your eye. At the game's zoom 1 (64 px per hex) most nature features are only a few pixels: trees, hedges and the pond read, the boulders, the dry-stone wall (nature-13) and the fence posts (nature-15) are specks, and the pale rock outcrop (nature-11) is the brightest small thing on the board. If you want the features to read at zoom 1, round 2 should paint them about one and a half times larger. Nothing reads as woods (the biggest is a clump of three crowns) and nothing reads as a site; the homesteads are deliberately field-free, but home-07 (L-shaped farmhouse with a walled yard) and roadside turn_n_se-B (kitchen garden in rows) come closest to the farm and are not in my picks. The h1-a houses (home-08, home-09) have paler walls and red roofs, a little brighter than the slate-roofed h1-b set but closer to the town tiles' roofs. Roadside variants exist for straights and turns only; forks, ends and hills roads keep the shipped tiles. A homestead tile has no road, so beside a road it sits in its own field rather than facing the road; only the roadside tiles relate buildings to a road.

Applying it would mean: copy the picked files into frontend/src/board/tiles/ under new folders the cosmetic glob does not mix into the plain variants (for example tiles/plains_nature/NN.png, tiles/plains_home/NN.png, and road variants as tiles/road_variety/plains_<shape>_NN.png; the shipped plains and road groups stay as they are), port variety_picks from scripts/board-mock.py (salted_index, the per-mille rolls, the rank rule and the per-map pass) into frontend/src/board/hexTile.ts beside the lake masks, with the site footprints passed in from the world view, and add a parity fixture like the lake tiles have: a script writes the picks for a few exported windows to frontend/src/board/__fixtures__/variety.json and a Vitest test checks the TypeScript port against it, plus a byte-copy sync test like test_lake_tiles_sync.py. Provenance and replay are in art/codex/terrain/candidates/variety-r1/ (candidates.json names the sheet, cell, raw and gates of every tile) and art/codex/terrain/README.md.
